source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
To recap, the factory tested all 3 boards: 1 works and has L3 stable at 3.3V, while the other 2 fluctuate between 0.5–2V. That suggests the design is fine and that those 2 may have an AXP2101 thermal-pad soldering problem.

The factory uses a completely automated process with a stencil + reflow oven and no hand soldering. I reviewed the gerbers, and the 13 tented GND vias beneath the pad appear fine. However, the paste aperture for the AXP2101 thermal pad is one full, unsegmented opening. Could excessive paste cause the chip to float in the reflow oven and make inconsistent ground contact? Would dividing that pad into a segmented "windowpane" paste aperture improve the yield?
What is your opinion?

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the full, unsegmented thermal-pad paste aperture causes excessive solder and inconsistent AXP2101 attachment, and whether a segmented windowpane aperture is required.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I noticed one additional detail that may support this theory. According to the factory, VBUS and VSYS are normal on all 3 boards, and all of those pins are located along the top edge of the AXP2101. The DCDC1 pins—FB1, LX1, and VIN1—are all on the right edge, which is precisely the side that fails on the 2 defective boards. This makes it seem as though the chip tilts during reflow: the top edge remains connected while the right edge lifts. That is why I suspect the single full paste opening beneath the center pad may be depositing too much solder and causing the chip to float. Is that consistent with what you would expect, and can you update the stencil to a windowpane pattern on your side?

source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

They examined the chip by x ray and found that it was properly welded. They then reported the following:

I have inspected the AP2101 already and found no indication of poor welding. When these two boards were powered on, the positive terminal of the L3 capacitor became shorted to GND.

execution.observed_behavior: Factory X-ray inspection found the AXP2101 properly soldered with no indication of poor welding, refuting thermal-pad attachment as the observed failure mode on the inspected boards.
